html:
The Battle of Viipuri was fought from 24 to 29 April 1918 in Viipuri, now Vyborg in Russia, then one of the largest cities of Finland. The White army took the last stronghold of the Reds, which decided the Finnish Civil War.

Finland, until then a grand duchy under the Russian tsar, declared independence in December 1917, after the Russian Revolution. In January 1918 Finnish socialists, the Reds, took Helsinki and the industrial south, helped by Soviet Russia. The conservative government's army, the Whites, held the north under General Gustaf Mannerheim, and Germany sent troops to help it. In April the Whites took Tampere and the Germans took Helsinki. The Red leaders moved to Viipuri, near the Russian border. About 18,500 Whites cut the railway to Petrograd and stormed the town. Most Red leaders escaped by sea to Russia.

After the victory White soldiers shot hundreds of prisoners and civilians, among them up to 400 Russians and others who had taken no part. Over 11,000 Reds were captured. About 36,000 people died in it, many in prison camps. Finland stayed independent and did not become a Soviet republic. The Soviet Union took Vyborg in the wars of 1939 to 1944.
